from.place: Proof opening: Choose a compactification c=(j,p); the local compact-support-extension and cofiltered-coherent-diagram splits require coherent comparisons of this choice. This is an agent-added foundation, not a WANTED quotation from the blueprint.

proof.text: First prove the final-edge converse without using any forward implication. Suppose $u:X\to Y$ has the stated $\Lambda_n^n$ extension property. The $\Lambda_2^2$ with vertices $(Y,X,Y)$ and edges $02=\mathrm{id}_Y$, $12=u$ fills to a triangle $\tau$ with $01=v:Y\to X$ and $uv\simeq\mathrm{id}_Y$. On vertices $(X,Y,X,Y)$ prescribe faces $d_0=\tau$, $d_1=s_0u$ and $d_2=s_1u$. Their common edges agree: the edges $13$ and $03$ are $\mathrm{id}_Y$ and $u$, respectively, and $23=u$. They therefore define a map on $\Lambda_3^3$, with final edge $u$. Its filler has missing face $d_3$ with edges $(u,v,\mathrm{id}_X)$, giving $vu\simeq\mathrm{id}_X$. Thus the same $v$ supplies both inverse triangles required by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Proof of (3) implies (1), with the three tetrahedral faces written explicitly; face gluing is degreewise gluing of the horn union.

proof.text: Use the join and the weakly saturated class of inner anodyne maps defined in [lem-coef-infinity-pushout-join-saturation]. A quasicategory $Q$ extends maps across every inner anodyne inclusion. Indeed it extends across the generating inner horns by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Extension is preserved by pushout: glue the old map and the extension on the attached piece. It is preserved by transfinite composition: choose an extension at each successor and use the degreewise colimit at each limit ordinal. For an arrow retract $i:A\to B$ of $j:A^\prime\to B^\prime$, write its section as $(s_A,s_B)$ and retraction as $(r_A,r_B)$, so $r_As_A=\mathrm{id}_A$ and $s_Bi=js_A$. Given $f:A\to Q$, extend $fr_A$ across $j$ to $g:B^\prime\to Q$; then $gs_Bi=gjs_A=fr_As_A=f$. Thus $gs_B$ is the extension across $i$. Isomorphisms are immediate. These arguments prove the required closure directly, without a model structure or an outer-horn theorem.

source.place: Meaning of inner anodyneness in the proof of Proposition 4.3.6.4; elementary extension-closure argument.

proof.text: Fix a left horn $k:\Lambda_i^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, where $m\geq1$ and $0\leq i<m$. For the boundary inclusion $a:\partial\Delta^p\hookrightarrow\Delta^p$, $p\geq0$, the pushout-join $\theta_{a,k}$ of [lem-coef-infinity-pushout-join-saturation] is exactly $\Lambda_{p+1+i}^{p+m+1}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{p+m+1}$. To check this, order the $p+1$ vertices of the first factor before those of the second. The first summand of the attaching union supplies all faces omitting a first-factor vertex; the second supplies all faces omitting a second-factor vertex except vertex $p+1+i$. This accounts for every included simplex as well, since each is characterized by its omitted vertices. The omitted index is inner: $0<p+1+i<p+m+1$. For $p=0$ the first boundary is empty and the same face calculation holds. For this fixed $k$, the cited saturation lemma says that the class of monomorphisms $a$ making $\theta_{a,k}$ inner anodyne is weakly saturated. The boundary-cell decomposition of [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] consequently puts every monomorphism $a:A\hookrightarrow B$ in this class: well-order each set of attached cells, attach them successively by pushouts, and take the union over dimensions. Hence $(A\star\Delta^m)\cup_{A\star\Lambda_i^m}(B\star\Lambda_i^m)\hookrightarrow B\star\Delta^m$ is inner anodyne for every such $a$ and $k$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.4, left-horn version of the generating calculation and weak-saturation reduction; boundary generation is 0077.

proof.text: For a small simplicial set $K$ and $f:K\to Q$, define the coslice $Q_{f/}$ by $(Q_{f/})_r=\{h:K\star\Delta^r\to Q\mid h|_K=f\}$, with operators precomposition on the second join factor. For a nonempty simplicial set $T$, a map $T\to Q_{f/}$ is equivalently a map $K\star T\to Q$ fixed as $f$ on $K$: its maps $K\star\Delta^r\to Q$ for each simplex of $T$ agree on all faces and degeneracies and glue degree by degree by the displayed join formula; restriction to each simplex gives the inverse construction. Let $K_0\subseteq K$ and $f_0=f|_{K_0}$. A lifting square for restriction $\rho:Q_{f/}\to Q_{f_0/}$ against $\Lambda_i^m\subseteq\Delta^m$ specifies precisely a map on $(K_0\star\Delta^m)\cup(K\star\Lambda_i^m)$ restricting to $f$ on $K$. Steps 2 and 3 extend this map to $K\star\Delta^m$ when $0\leq i<m$, and the extension still restricts to $f$. Thus $\rho$ is a left fibration, meaning it lifts these horns over the prescribed base simplex. Taking $K_0=\varnothing$ gives a left fibration $Q_{f/}\to Q$, since $\varnothing\star\Delta^r=\Delta^r$. Each coslice is a quasicategory: fill the image of an inner horn in $Q$, then lift that chosen filler along its projection. This proves the coslice facts needed below inside this proof, rather than citing the much larger cone-calculus theorem.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.8, absolute coslice restriction, proved here using its pushout-join lifting argument; projection is the empty-subset case (018F).

proof.text: Here are the two left-fibration consequences used below, with actual inverse triangles. Let $p:E\to B$ lift the horns $\Lambda_i^m$ with $0\leq i<m$, and let $E,B$ be quasicategories. Suppose $a:x\to y$ maps to an equivalence. Choose an inverse $b:p(y)\to p(x)$. Lift its triangle $b\,p(a)\simeq\mathrm{id}_{p(x)}$ using $\Lambda_0^2$ with edges $01=a$, $02=\mathrm{id}_x$, obtaining a triangle $\tau=(a,c,\mathrm{id}_x)$ with $p(c)=b$. Repeat with $c$ and an inverse triangle for $b$ to get $\sigma=(c,e,\mathrm{id}_y)$ for some $e:x\to y$. To obtain the second inverse triangle for the SAME $c$, use three inner tetrahedral horns in $E$. On vertices $(x,y,x,y)$ prescribe $d_0=\sigma$, $d_1=s_0e$, $d_3=\tau$ and fill $\Lambda_2^3$; its face $H=d_2$ has edges $(a,\mathrm{id}_y,e)$. On $(x,y,y,y)$ prescribe $d_0$ constant at $y$, $d_2=s_1a$, $d_3=H$ and fill $\Lambda_1^3$; its face $H'=d_1$ has edges $(e,\mathrm{id}_y,a)$. On $(y,x,y,y)$ prescribe $d_0=H'$, $d_1$ constant at $y$, $d_3=\sigma$ and fill $\Lambda_2^3$; its face $d_2$ has edges $(c,a,\mathrm{id}_y)$. In each horn the displayed triangles have identical edges on their pairwise overlaps. Together with $\tau$, this proves that $a$ is an equivalence, so $p$ reflects equivalences. Separately, if $v:b_0\to p(y)$ is an equivalence and $y\in E$ is prescribed, lift an inverse $v^{-1}$ starting at $y$ using $\Lambda_0^1=\{0\}$, obtaining $t:y\to z$. Lift the inverse triangle $v v^{-1}\simeq\mathrm{id}_{p(y)}$ using $\Lambda_0^2$ with edges $01=t$, $02=\mathrm{id}_y$. Its edge $12:z\to y$ lies exactly over $v$. This gives the needed lift with prescribed target, without claiming target lifts for arbitrary base edges.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.2.11, two lifted left-inverse triangles. The three displayed inner tetrahedral horns expand the homotopy cancellation into actual inverse-triangle witnesses. Specified-target lifting is a left 1- and 2-horn calculation.

proof.text: Now let $\sigma_0:\Lambda_n^n\to Q$, $n\geq2$, have equivalence final edge $u$. Put $K=\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,n-2\}}$, $K_0=\partial K$, and $f=\sigma_0|_K$. Here $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$. In the ordered join $K\star\Delta^{\{n-1,n\}}=\Delta^n$, the given horn is the union $(K\star\{n\})\cup(K_0\star\Delta^{\{n-1,n\}})$. Indeed its faces are all those omitting a vertex $j<n$: $j=n-1$ gives the first piece, and $j<n-1$ gives the second. The first restriction of $\sigma_0$ defines an object $Y$ of $Q_{f/}$. The second defines an edge $\bar v:\bar X\to\rho(Y)$ in $Q_{f_0/}$, with image $u$ under the projection to $Q$. By step 4, both $\rho:Q_{f/}\to Q_{f_0/}$ and this projection are left fibrations between quasicategories. Step 5 makes $\bar v$ an equivalence, then lifts it along $\rho$ with target exactly $Y$. By the definition in step 4, the lifted edge is a map $K\star\Delta^1\to Q$ agreeing with $\sigma_0$ on both pieces of the displayed union. It is the required filler on $\Delta^n$. For $n=2$, the union is the two edges $02$ and $12$, the base coslice is $Q$ itself, and the same construction applies.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.4.2.13 specialized to Q -> point, with the horn union and prescribed-target lift expanded. The actual left-fibration and conservativity assertions were proved in steps 2-5.

proof.text: Finally reverse the simplex orders. Explicitly the involution on the simplex category takes $\alpha:[r]\to[s]$ to $\alpha^{\mathrm{rev}}(j)=s-\alpha(r-j)$; precomposition defines $Q^{\mathrm{op}}$. On standard simplices this changes face $i$ to face $n-i$, and therefore identifies the opposite of $\Lambda_0^n\subseteq\Delta^n$ with $\Lambda_n^n\subseteq\Delta^n$. Inner indices remain inner, so $Q^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a quasicategory. An inverse edge and its two inverse triangles become an inverse edge and the two reversed triangles, so equivalence is preserved and reflected. Apply the final-horn forward implication of step 6 in $Q^{\mathrm{op}}$ and reverse again to fill every initial horn in $Q$ whose edge $01$ is an equivalence. Apply the final-horn converse of step 1 in $Q^{\mathrm{op}}$ to obtain the initial-horn converse in $Q$. This supplies both orientations and both converses for all $n\geq2$.

source.place: The proof says the initial-edge version is analogous; explicit order-reversal realizes that duality without any extra categorical theorem.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 4.4.2.6 via Proposition 4.4.2.13 (01H0); the coslice lifting argument is expanded using 018J, 0077 and 01BZ. Reflection follows 019K with its inverse algebra expanded into three inner tetrahedral horns. Online sources read; archival copies WANTED in report.md.

title: Outer horn fillers along an equivalence
statement: Use horns and equivalence edges as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $Q$ be a quasicategory and $n\geq2$. Every map $\Lambda_0^n\to Q$ whose edge $[0,1]$ is an equivalence extends to $\Delta^n$. Every map $\Lambda_n^n\to Q$ whose edge $[n-1,n]$ is an equivalence also extends to $\Delta^n$. Conversely, an edge having either of these extension properties for every such horn is an equivalence.

source.place: Theorem 4.4.2.6 (Joyal), equivalence of (1), (2), (3). These are Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags.
